title: Greece drafts legislation requiring data centers source 60% of power from renewables
key_facts: Greece's Ministry of Environment and Energy drafted a law requiring new data centers to meet at least 60% of annual electricity use with renewables.
Investors would pay grid connection and reinforcement costs and post a bank guarantee of 200,000 euros per MW of planned capacity.
Data center investors face financial capacity checks, and a registry would track the sector.
The draft also proposes quarterly publication of available grid capacity and flexible connections, plus a 2.3 billion euro Island Decarbonization Fund.
The draft is open to public consultation until 24 Oct 2026.
Similar efforts exist in Spain, Australia, Brazil and Massachusetts.
quote_evidence: Greece wants new data centers to meet at least 60% of their annual electricity demand with renewable energy under draft rules aimed at improving electricity market design.
The draft legislation is open for public consultation until October 24, 2026.
why_it_matters_hint: Governments are starting to make data centers pay for and green the power they use.
